items.title: NBA off to best viewership yet for non-lockout season, buoyed by young demo increases
items.summary: In year two of its new media rights setup, the NBA is averaging 2.62 million viewers across NBC, ESPN, Prime Video and NBA TV, its best non-lockout season pace on record and up 37% on the same point last season. The Emirates NBA Cup is averaging 2 million viewers on Prime Video, up 90%, while viewers aged 18-34 are up 50% and 12-17 are up 57%, and about 25% of national TV viewers are now under 35. Live game and content viewing across the NBA App and League Pass is up 50%, the Tap to Watch effort drove 8 million live streams in the first month, and local games are up 24% across a mix of over-the-air, RSN and streaming deals.
items.what_it_means: Spreading games across broadcast and streaming partners is coinciding with a younger, larger national audience for the NBA.

items.title: Meta inks 49ers sponsorship, will give away AI glasses
items.summary: The 49ers have signed Meta to a multiyear partnership in a new category, 'official moment maker', centred on its AI glasses. The launch activation gives Oakley Meta HSTN glasses, which usually sell for $399 or more, to more than 4,700 suite holders and club season ticket holders for the franchise's 80th anniversary. WhatsApp becomes the team's official instant messenger provider to support its marketing in the UK, UAE and Mexico under the NFL's global markets programme, and Meta also presents the Salute to Service campaign and gets digital signage at Levi's Stadium.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are buying categories built around fan behaviour, putting product in the hands of a team's most valuable ticket holders.

items.title: NFL's Hans Schroeder: More big changes coming to sports rights market
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers event, NFL chief media officer Hans Schroeder said more consolidation and ownership changes are likely among rights holders, after two of the league's seven live game partners were part of major transactions in 2026, and that sports content has never been more valuable. On the same stage, Bank of America analyst Jessica Reif Ehrlich predicted Walmart would be big in sports rights acquisitions in 2027. Schroeder also said he is preparing for the pay-TV universe to bottom out, which MoffettNathanson puts at about 50 million households in 2030, and ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said ESPN would like World Series rights when Fox's deal ends after 2028.
items.what_it_means: The buyers of sports rights are changing, with retailers named alongside media companies and the pay-TV bundle nearing a floor.

items.title: Pinehurst, Titleist seeing early returns on new retail location
items.summary: The Titleist Shop at Pinehurst Resort, the first location of its kind in the US, opened in autumn 2025 next to the driving range, a departure from Titleist's usual reliance on big-box stores and pro shops. With 450,000 to 500,000 rounds a year at the resort, it has printed custom logos on more than 2,000 dozen balls, sold more than 600 Scotty Cameron putters and nearly 500 Vokey wedges, and lifted club fittings from about 200 a year to more than 700 by mid-November. Pinehurst's Eric Kuester compares it to an Apple store, and the resort keeps all the revenue.
items.what_it_means: A venue that already hosts the fan's experience can turn a sponsor into an on-site store, with exclusives that only work in that place.

items.title: How Trackhouse Racing helps VIPs talk to cars, literally
items.summary: NASCAR team Trackhouse Racing built an app for guests in its pit box that sends race updates from a persona of Connor Zilisch's No. 88 car, called 88Bot, drawn from race-day data. The team hosts 30 to 60 VIPs a race, including families, partners and prospective sponsors, and owner Justin Marks said technology has become a mandate in the business to make the guest experience as vital as the racing. Trackhouse worked with digital design firm Very Good Ventures from mid-2024, testing in the few hours before each race and handling roughly 25,000 data messages a second.
items.what_it_means: Teams are using their own live data to make hospitality more valuable for partners and prospective sponsors.

items.title: PGA Tour Fall Ends With Ticket Fiasco After Weather Disruption
items.summary: Heavy rain cancelled Saturday play at the RSM Classic at Sea Island, pushing the third round to Sunday and the final round to Monday. Saturday tickets, from $65 general admission to nearly $600 for the Skybox Club, were not honoured on Sunday and no fans were allowed in on Monday, with organisers citing safe capacity and limited volunteers. Fans learned through social media that refunds were not on offer, comments on the tournament's post were turned off, and organisers later said they would contact Saturday ticket holders directly.
items.what_it_means: When an event is disrupted, the refund and communication policy becomes the fan experience, and silence on social compounds the damage.

items.title: Canada's TD Coliseum celebrates 'tremendous' first year post-$300m renovation
items.summary: Oak View Group's TD Coliseum in Hamilton, Ontario, drew more than 850,000 fans to 110 events in its first year after a C$300 million renovation, with acts including Cardi B, Smashing Pumpkins and Katseye. The 18,000-capacity arena, about 70km from Toronto, added a rigging grid, acoustic panelling, a bigger open floor, premium suites and a purpose-built artist compound. Pollstar's mid-year rankings put it as the top-selling venue in the Canadian market, and 75% of ticket buyers came from outside the Hamilton area.
items.what_it_means: A rebuilt arena outside a major city can pull most of its audience from elsewhere, if it is built to win tours.

items.title: Novo signs on as 76ers corporate sponsor
items.summary: Novo, maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, has signed as a 76ers sponsor with presenting rights to an online content series plus social, digital and arena signage. Activation includes a 'First Step Sweepstakes' where fans pledge to complete healthy activities for a chance to win Sixers experiences and merchandise. Novo has been quiet in US sports apart from a cycling team, the Hurricanes and UNC, and the 76ers have signed more than a dozen new sponsors out of 23 during their resurgence.
items.what_it_means: A new category of sponsor is entering US sport through content and fan participation rather than signage alone.

items.title: How Joya Studio brought the scents of A24's 'Backrooms' into consumers' own rooms
items.summary: Fragrance house Joya Studio released a 'scent score' for A24's Backrooms, five bespoke smells designed to be sprayed at set timestamps while watching at home, plus a candle of the final scent. It launched as the film moved into its streaming window at the end of September, giving viewers a reason to revisit a film that has taken $400 million worldwide, A24's biggest success. Preorders sold out quickly.
items.what_it_means: Entertainment brands are designing products that make the at-home window an event in its own right.

items.title: Sanjay Govil is taking a big swing at cricket in the U.S.
items.summary: Washington Freedom owner Sanjay Govil, one of several tech founders backing Major League Cricket alongside Satya Nadella and Shantanu Narayen, says around 40 million people watch cricket in the US. The league is building its own grounds, including Pomona, California, which will host Olympic cricket in 2028, and a Frederick, Maryland pitch opening next year as the league grows from six to eight teams. Govil said the month-long season needs to expand, awareness has lagged, and the right media deal should be measured by accessibility as well as money.
items.what_it_means: A new league with an existing diaspora audience is prioritising venues, a longer season and reach before rights fees.
